1.o: This chapter is the description of a lamentable devastation made of the country of Judah by locusts and caterpillars. Some think that the prophet speaks of it as a thing to come and gives warning of it beforehand, as usually the prophets did of judgments coming. Others think that it was now present, and that his business was to affect the people with it and awaken them by it to repentance. I. It is spoken of as a judgment which there was no precedent of in former ages, ver. 1-7. II.
1.s: Locusts and the Day of the Lord
1.i: Joel 1 and 3 give the book's two ends: a swarm of locusts, and the Lord who dwells in Zion.
1.p: Lord, be our refuge. Teach us to turn to You in hard times and to tell our children what You did. Amen.
1.l: Tell someone younger than you about a hard time you got through, so that the story is passed on.
q: Joel tells people to pass the story down. What story in your family should be passed down?

2.o: In this chapter we have, I. A further description of that terrible desolation which should be made in the land of Judah by the locusts and caterpillars, ver. 1-11. II. A serious call to the people, when they are under this sore judgment, to return and repent, to fast and pray, and to seek unto God for mercy, with directions how to do this aright, ver. 12-17. III.

3.o: In the close of the foregoing chapter we had a gracious promise of deliverance in Mount Zion and Jerusalem; now this whole chapter is a comment upon that promise, showing what that deliverance shall be, how it shall be wrought by the destruction of the church's enemies, and how it shall be perfected in the everlasting rest and joy of the church.
